equation_summary: HGRN keeps a VECTOR state h[B,D] with a per-channel data-dependent forget gate: h_t = exp(f_t) * h_{t-1} + i_t, and the output o_t = h_t (the state is read out directly each step). f = logsigmoid(f_proj(x)) (optionally lower-bounded via logaddexp), and i = swiglu(i_proj(x), 1 - exp(f)). There is no q/k/v and no matrix state; it is a channel-gated vector recurrence, not a matrix-valued linear-delta law.
ledger_verdicts: CONFIRM B[K2 vector gated transition]: HGRN is a vector-state, channel-gated additive recurrence, not the matrix [K,V] U2.A law
CONFIRM 'matrix-A is not assumed': the ledger correctly does NOT claim this is U2.A; it flags a distinct vector gated transition descriptor
CONFIRM blockers: read/update order (after-update, o_t = h_t) and vector-state VJP
axis: A-vec channel-gated vector state transition (vector K2)
direction_justification: HGRN's mixer is a vector-valued channel-gated recurrence h_t = exp(f_t)⊙h_{t-1} + i_t with o_t = h_t; this is a different state shape (vector, no key/value outer product) than the canonical matrix K2 law, so it needs a closed vector-state descriptor rather than plain U2.A.
open_questions: Whether the vector-state gated transition generalizes to a second client; HGRN2 moves to a matrix GLA state, so HGRN may be a single-client axis and could be kept external-only if no second client materializes.
